wordings.idea: A dispute can be settled by distinguishing the different practical senses of the contested term, so that both parties are right in one sense and wrong in the other
quotes: Mindful of the scholastic adage that whenever you meet a contradiction you must make a distinction, I immediately sought and found one, as follows: "Which party is right," I said, "depends on what you PRACTICALLY MEAN by 'going round' the squirrel.
Make the distinction, and there is no occasion for any farther dispute.
You are both right and both wrong according as you conceive the verb 'to go round' in one practical fashion or the other."
wordings.why: The kept notes cover only the case where no practical difference exists and the dispute is idle. Without this item, the second use of the method is lost: an ambiguous term hides several practical meanings, and separating them dissolves the dispute.

   - Quote: "Mindful of the scholastic adage that whenever you meet a contradiction you must make a distinction, I immediately sought and found one, as follows: "Which party is right," I said, "depends on what you PRACTICALLY MEAN by 'going round' the squirrel."
   - Quote: "Make the distinction, and there is no occasion for any farther dispute."
   - Quote: "You are both right and both wrong according as you conceive the verb 'to go round' in one practical fashion or the other.""
   - Why: The kept notes cover only the case where no practical difference exists and the dispute is idle. Without this item, the second use of the method is lost: an ambiguous term hides several practical meanings, and separating them dissolves the dispute.

wordings.idea: A dispute can dissolve by distinguishing the different practical senses of a term, leaving both sides right and wrong depending on which sense they mean
quotes: Which party is right," I said, "depends on what you PRACTICALLY MEAN by 'going round' the squirrel.
Make the distinction, and there is no occasion for any farther dispute.
You are both right and both wrong according as you conceive the verb 'to go round' in one practical fashion or the other.
wordings.why: The kept notes cover only disputes with no practical difference between the alternatives, which are idle. This is a second way the method settles disputes: the practical meanings differ but the disputants were using different ones. The notes never say this, and the squirrel case is the only place it is stated.
